inputs.notes: Net debt is negative (net cash position). Q1 2026 cash $45.1M, effectively zero debt. Shares: 27.7M diluted. Base FCF is FY2025 actuals.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 FCF of $62.93m retained as the base. Q2-2026 CONFIRMS the model rather than contradicting it: H1 revenue $260.4m (+14.0% YoY) against the base case's 13% Year-1 assumption, Q2 +14.7%, and H1 operating cash flow $38.2m (+22.7%). H1 free cash flow is NEGATIVE $36.7m only because capex jumped to $74.8m from $1.9m -- $61.3m of that is four San Antonio properties (land, buildings, and a vacant building in CIP) plus $12.9m of manufacturing equipment due in service in 2027. This is the buildout the Year-1 12.0% FCF margin already anticipated, and it is a step-change, not a new run rate.

historical_growth.fcf_note: FCF 3yr CAGR is distorted because FY2022 FCF was only $4.1M (working capital absorption year). FY2021-FY2025 4yr CAGR is 52.8%, also distorted by FCF lumpiness. The 5yr CAGR of 30.4% is more meaningful but still inflated by operational maturation. Trend is directionally correct: FCF is on a secular uptrend as capex normalizes.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Equity CAGR is inflated by retained earnings compounding rapidly on a small base and not meaningful as a standalone rate. FCF CAGRs are distorted by base-year lumpiness. Revenue 3yr CAGR of 13.7% best represents current normalized growth trajectory as the 5yr includes the hyper-growth 2020-2021 COVID rebound period. DCF uses FCF-margin-based projections anchored to revenue trajectory rather than a single selected growth rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (31.0%) diverges significantly from Revenue 3yr CAGR (13.7%) and EPS 3yr CAGR (7.2%), driven by high retention ratio on growing profits. Not a red flag for XPEL — equity is compounding via retained earnings with minimal buybacks. FCF margin approach used for projections is more reliable than equity-based growth extrapolation here.

base.narrative: Revenue grows at roughly current trajectory, decelerating from ~13% to ~8% over 5 years as the law of large numbers sets in. FCF margins are modestly below the FY2025 level in Year 1 (12.0%) due to $110M manufacturing capex and China integration headwinds, recovering gradually to 16.5% by Year 5 as vertical integration partially delivers. WACC 10.5% reflects US small-cap premium plus modest risk premium for supplier concentration, China execution, and manufacturing buildout. Terminal growth 3.0% for a durable niche compounder in a still-growing global market.
base.fcf_margin_rationale: FY2025 FCF margin was 13.2% (62.93/476.2). Near-term dip to 12.0% in Y1 due to capex ramp and China integration costs. Partial credit for manufacturing margin recovery by Year 3-5 — management targets 52-54% gross margin by 2028 vs. ~42% today; base case haircuts this to roughly half the expansion materializing within the 5-year window.

bull.narrative: Manufacturing vertical integration thesis succeeds and delivers gross margin expansion toward 50%+ by Year 4-5. China scales meaningfully — OEM and 4S dealership channels add $80-100M+ incremental revenue. DAP software lock-in accelerates installer base growth. PPF attach rates on new vehicles rise from sub-10% toward 15%+. Revenue grows 18-11% over 5 years. FCF margins expand from 13% to 21.5% as operating leverage kicks in.
bull.fcf_margin_rationale: Bull case assumes manufacturing buildout delivers ~10pp gross margin expansion by Year 4-5 (toward 52%), SG&A leverage on higher revenue base, and China direct-to-market adds high-margin incremental revenue. FCF margin of 21.5% by Y5 equates to roughly 26-27% operating margin, consistent with management's mid-to-high 20% target if achieved.

bear.narrative: Margin recovery stalls — petrochemical cost pressures, manufacturing execution delays, and elevated SG&A mean FCF margins are flat or declining. China regulatory friction limits market contribution. Auto market softness reduces installer demand and dealership throughput. Revenue decelerates sharply to low single digits. Capex weighs heavily on FCF conversion near-term.
bear.fcf_margin_rationale: Bear case assumes manufacturing capex consumes FCF benefits, supplier pricing power limits gross margin recovery, and a mild auto market downturn pressures revenue mix. FCF margin stays in the 10.5-12% range — below FY2025 actuals — reflecting elevated fixed cost absorption during the transition.

base.note: Entry price at which an investor would earn 15% CAGR to terminal value. Current price of $45.84 implies approximately 6.8% CAGR to terminal value in base case.

bull.note: In bull case, current price of $45.84 offers 22.6% CAGR to terminal value — well above the 15% hurdle.

bear.note: In bear case, current price implies significant capital loss. The bear case reflects a scenario where the manufacturing thesis fails and margins stagnate.

sensitivity.matrix_description: Rows = WACC (8.5% to 12.5%), Columns = Terminal Growth Rate (2.0% to 4.0%). All values are intrinsic value per share in USD using base case FCF projections. Base case (WACC 10.5%, TGR 3.0%) = $52.73.

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Equal weighting to bull and bear at 25% each, 50% base. Reflects meaningful upside optionality from manufacturing thesis (bull scenario not fully discounted at current price) balanced against real execution risk in the bear scenario. Current price of $45.84 sits between base ($52.73) and bear ($26.19), closer to the base case.

sanity_checks.assessment: Base case intrinsic value of $52.73 implies 28.5x trailing P/E and ~18.6x EV/EBITDA — both squarely within XPEL's ex-bubble historical trading range of 27-30x P/E and 17-20x EV/EBITDA. This is NOT a compressed multiple requiring heroic assumptions; it is a defensible conservative estimate for a quality compounder with strong FCF generation. Current market price of $45.84 (24.8x trailing P/E) represents a ~15% discount to base case IV, indicating modest undervaluation with significant upside in the bull scenario.

investment_summary.thesis: XPEL is a durable niche compounder transitioning from asset-light distribution to vertically integrated manufacturing. The $110M strategic investment announced May 2026 is the central near-term catalyst — success would expand gross margins from ~42% to 52-54% by 2028, nearly doubling operating margins and materially expanding EPS and FCF. The stock trades at a modest discount to base case IV ($45.84 vs. $52.73) and at a meaningful discount to probability-weighted IV ($57.90). The entry price for a 15% CAGR hurdle rate in the base case ($31.74) suggests the current price does not offer a margin of safety for deep value investors, but the risk/reward is favorable for growth-at-reasonable-price (GARP) investors with a 3-5 year horizon.
key_risks: Manufacturing buildout execution risk — margin expansion delayed to 2027-2028 at earliest
China regulatory and geopolitical exposure (12% of revenue and growing)
Supplier concentration during manufacturing transition window (2026-2027)
Consumer discretionary sensitivity — PPF is a premium vehicle add-on
key_catalysts: Q2/Q3 2026 gross margin recovery as China high-cost inventory normalizes
Manufacturing facility milestones in San Antonio and China
China OEM and 4S dealership revenue growth trajectory
FCF conversion improvement confirming capex peak is behind

sanity_check_verdict.reason: Weighted IV $57.9 vs $50.69 (+14.2%). Model confirmed by Q2-2026, not rebuilt.
sanity_check_verdict.value_investor_conclusion: The Q2 print supports the thesis. Whether it is a BUY depends on the margin recovery to 16.5% by Year 5, which is the single load-bearing assumption and is not yet evidenced.

valuation_philosophy:
Reviewed 2026-08-28 against Q2-2026 and LEFT SUBSTANTIALLY UNCHANGED -- the only model in this session's audit that survived contact with fresh actuals. Revenue is running +14.0% in H1 against a 13% Year-1 assumption; gross margin improved to 44.1% from 42.9% on lower product costs, mix and the sell-through of higher-cost inventory from the China distributor acquisition; and the negative H1 free cash flow is the manufacturing capex ramp the model explicitly built in. China revenue more than doubled in Q2 (+106.7%) on that acquisition, while Europe declined slightly and India/Middle East fell 5.0%, both attributed to distributor timing and the Iran conflict. Scenario assumptions untouched.

THREE THINGS A PRE-Q2 MODEL DID NOT HAVE, all reflected in the inputs rather than the scenarios: (1) the first material debt in the company's history -- a $44.8m PNC term loan at SOFR+125bp secured on the San Antonio properties -- so the ~$50.8m net cash position at December is now roughly $4.1m of NET DEBT; (2) a new 75%-owned China manufacturing subsidiary ($21.4m, purchase accounting preliminary) which introduces a minority interest a prior model would not deduct; (3) sales and marketing growing 29.7% against revenue at 14.7%, so some operating leverage is being spent rather than banked. None of these changes the thesis; all of them narrow the margin for error. The load-bearing assumption remains the FCF-margin recovery to 16.5% by Year 5, which is still unevidenced.
